Great food, but disappointed by the water policy
Jul 2025 • Family
We had a really good dinner here — tasty food, pleasant atmosphere, and friendly service.

However, I was surprised (and honestly disappointed) to be told that the only water option was an expensive Italian bottled brand. In a Spanish restaurant, this felt completely out of place — and especially odd given the high quality of everything else. If water must be sold, at least offer a Spanish brand to stay in theme, or better yet, provide filtered or tap water like many good restaurants do.

Just to be clear — we weren’t trying to save money. We ordered wine and beer, and we were here to enjoy the full experience. But being forced to buy imported bottled water, while the table next to us (locals) received complimentary water, left a bad impression. It felt like a cheap upsell tactic, which this restaurant honestly doesn’t need.

It’s worth noting that the Chocolate café downstairs (Maison Marou) offers water the moment you sit down — a simple gesture that feels welcoming and respectful.

I hope the owner, knowing the standards of Dutch and European hospitality, considers changing this policy. It’s a small detail, but one that really affects the overall guest experience.

They made food, fun again.
Oct 2023 • Family
Second time here, brought the kids along this time.
Thankful that it weren't crowded - so the kids were able to roam around a little.
The live band and singer helped spruce up the mood and our little ones loved it.
The pretty and glittery bar aside, the tapas that we ordered were all fun and different from most other restaurants, even other Spanish tapas restaurants, and that sense of intrigue at the arrival of each dish just made the entire dining experience more fun. The servers were also quick to help us at every turn and to explain each dish to us.
The restaurant also served us some free dessert for Vietnamese Women's Day.

Good experience overall. Well done.

Tapas restaurant rue du Docteur Calmette
Dec 2023 • Family
A beautiful combination of this Tapas restaurant between France which named the street, Spain and its cuisine and Ho Chi Minh City with its many tables. It is accessible by a narrow staircase which opens onto a large and pretty room, well air-conditioned and decorated in the colors of Spain, predominantly red. Even the music is there, present but discreet. The atmosphere is pleasant, the servers smiling even if they need to be asked. The menu is tempting with most of the dishes in photos. It's well presented, commented on by the waiter and the flavors are fine but some are really tiny, like the fried squid whose tiny portion is not worth sharing. His photo does not appear on the card.
For the same price we would have liked a little more filling.

Fun and comforting, Tapas portions
Apr 2021 • Couples
Pretty chill, open concept bar resto setting above Maison Marou choco. Most items are pretty authentic Spanish Tapas.

It was rare to find Angus beef tartar on a set lunch starters menu in HCMC but it's available here. Their "Pisto Manchego" was a simple, but probably unique twist of egg on toast with the addition of the Manchego (sheep) cheese.

Our mains of "Canelones" and "Tortilla abierta de morcilla y chorizo" were comforting and tasty, though they also felt like starters, as they had few slices of chorizo and sausage on an egg, kinda like half a portion of an American breakfast. Then again, quality VS quantity? You decide. The Catalan-style creme brulee was pretty normal. 

Would recommend this place for comforting Spanish Tapas flavours.
